body:
### Problem

I encountered this issue while using rust-analyzer and used Codex to reduce it to the self-contained reproduction below.

If `codeLens/resolve` returns `ContentModified`, the code-lens provider leaves the lens unresolved but marks its row as rendered. The unresolved lens reserves an empty virtual line, and subsequent redraws do not resolve it again. The line stays blank until a new `textDocument/codeLens` request is triggered by an unrelated operation such as `:edit`.

Related reports cover individual parts of this behavior but not this failure path:

- #16900 and #16904 suppress `ContentModified` notifications but do not recover a failed `codeLens/resolve` request.
- #18008 and #28228 recover a failed top-level `textDocument/codeLens` refresh.
- #38153 ignores stale successful resolve responses.
- #38352 redraws after a request completes, but the lens remains unresolved.
- #38782 retains previously rendered text while replacement lenses resolve; on initial display there is no previous text.

### Steps to reproduce using "nvim --clean -u minimal_init.lua"

Create `repro.fake`:

```text
target
below
```

Create `minimal_init.lua`:

```lua
vim.opt.swapfile = false
vim.filetype.add({ extension = { fake = 'fake' } })
vim.lsp.codelens.enable(true)

local resolve_count = 0

local function fake_server(dispatchers)
  local next_id = 0
  local closing = false

  local function respond(id, callback, notify_reply, err, result)
    vim.schedule(function()
      if notify_reply then
        notify_reply(id)
      end
      callback(err, result, id)
    end)
  end

  return {
    request = function(method, params, callback, notify_reply)
      next_id = next_id + 1
      local id = next_id

      if method == 'initialize' then
        respond(id, callback, notify_reply, nil, {
          capabilities = {
            codeLensProvider = { resolveProvider = true },
            textDocumentSync = 1,
          },
        })
      elseif method == 'textDocument/codeLens' then
        respond(id, callback, notify_reply, nil, {
          {
            range = {
              start = { line = 0, character = 0 },
              ['end'] = { line = 0, character = 6 },
            },
            data = { id = 'lens' },
          },
        })
      elseif method == 'codeLens/resolve' then
        resolve_count = resolve_count + 1
        if resolve_count == 1 then
          respond(id, callback, notify_reply, {
            code = vim.lsp.protocol.ErrorCodes.ContentModified,
            message = 'content modified',
          }, nil)
        else
          local resolved = vim.deepcopy(params)
          resolved.command = {
            command = 'fake.references',
            title = '1 reference',
          }
          respond(id, callback, notify_reply, nil, resolved)
        end
      elseif method == 'shutdown' then
        respond(id, callback, notify_reply, nil, vim.NIL)
      else
        respond(id, callback, notify_reply, nil, vim.NIL)
      end

      return true, id
    end,
    notify = function(method)
      if method == 'exit' then
        closing = true
        dispatchers.on_exit(0, 0)
      end
      return true
    end,
    is_closing = function()
      return closing
    end,
    terminate = function()
      closing = true
    end,
  }
end

vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd('FileType', {
  pattern = 'fake',
  callback = function()
    vim.lsp.start({
      name = 'fake-codelens',
      cmd = fake_server,
      root_dir = vim.uv.cwd(),
    })
  end,
})
```

A blank virtual line appears above `target` and remains blank. Run `:edit`; a second resolve request succeeds and the virtual line displays `1 reference`.

### Expected behavior

A failed `codeLens/resolve` request should not leave a permanent blank virtual line. Neovim should discard the empty placeholder or allow the lens to be resolved again.

### Nvim version (nvim -v)

v0.13.0-dev-1168+ga85cce90e3

### Language server name/version

rust-analyzer 1.98.0-nightly

### Operating system/version

macOS 26.5.1 (25F80)

### Log file

_No response_

comment_data.body:
IIRC, this issue mostly occurs with `rust-analyzer`. I’ve looked into its behavior before—it seems like an internal bug causes it to believe the file has been modified shortly after opening and starting analysis, even though the editor never touches it. Consequently, when resolving code lenses that were requested upon opening the file, it returns `ContentModified`.

Personally, I consider this by design rather than a bug. I think nvim should simply reflect what the LSP server sends. Attempting to strip away code lenses that the server already sent because they failed to resolve feels like papering over their bugs. I did consider displaying a fallback message like "resolve error" in such cases, but ultimately felt that reflecting the server's actual state is best, and the blank space is enough to signal to the user that "something went wrong."

From my (very limited) understanding of the lsp spec, the `codelens/resolve` request can fail. I don't know why rust analyzer sends that error for a first request, maybe they use it a bit liberally to signal that the codelens is not ready yet, but that doesn't matter.

From my perspective, nvim is leaving a bunch of empty lines that comes out of nowhere (I honestly took too much time to realize it was supposed to be the place for codelenses) and looks broken.

I would think that re-trying `codelens/resolve` is the right thing to do, but I don't have any idea why/if that can be difficult or an issue.

But even if we could "release" the empty virtual lines if the request fails, that would solve the issue of having the editor in a seemingly broken state, which I don't think is the responsibility of the language server because technically it is behaving according to spec.

When a server realizes an error has occurred, or finds that it cannot resolve a code lens it previously provided in response to `textDocument/codeLens`, the server can proactively have the editor refresh the entire area via `codeLens/refresh`. 

rust-analyzer uses this very approach. When the editor opens a file and sends a `textDocument/codeLens` request at the same time, it often cannot respond immediately and instead returns empty data (it could technically choose to defer the response until it is ready, but it doesn't, maybe limited by implementation). Later, it uses `codeLens/refresh` so that the actual results can be sent. However, this approach still fails to make up for some of its bugs.

That being said, Neovim could indeed proactively retry to confirm the intended results with the server after detecting faulty data, which would improve the user experience. Quoting my idea replied in #41248 here:

> One potential fix I considered is implementing a retry mechanism: if the buffer contains unresolved/malformed code lenses while the buffer remains unchanged, nvim could re-request them up to a maximum retry limit until the data becomes valid. 
>
> That said, it would be much cleaner to introduce this after we do a deeper refactor of `vim.lsp.Capability` (the layer managing automatic LSP data fetching for code lenses, inlay hints, etc.).
